purpose: Prior-edition (and current-2026) roster audit for the forward conference shortlist: who was actually in the room, and is the future edition worth the client's time for meeting owners of $5-50M US electrical-infrastructure service businesses.
method: Rosters pulled in full via free get_companies_in_list (page_size=100). Grata returns full detail only for the first 5 rows per page; all other rows are name+domain stubs, so classification is name/domain-driven analyst judgment (rule 1 applied: classify by what the company IS).

Categories: TARGET-PROFILE = US private electrical/power SERVICE company plausibly in/near $5-50M (oversized US service firms, PE platforms, foreign shops -> OTHER); ALREADY-KNOWN = domain in scripts/xref/known_keys.json dkeys (checked first, takes precedence); VENDOR/OEM/DISTRIBUTOR = sells product/software/insurance/staffing TO the trade; CUSTOMER-SIDE = utilities, co-ops, munis, gov, schools, ISOs, IPPs.
NET-NEW = target-profile domains in none of our lists (known_keys dkeys + conf_targets p2/all_candidates/master). Per-event display capped at 12; totals count all.

A hard deep-page block (HTTP 403) now sits at row 500 on every list: NECA LV 2026 (500/532), POWERGEN 2024 (500/595), IEEE PES T&D 2024 (500/1154), Utility Expo 2025 (500/1074) are truncated large-company-first, so small-company/target shares are understated on those events.

For the three sampled mega-rosters (POWERGEN, IEEE, Utility Expo) composition uses explicit t/c/o classification plus vendor-by-default for the unclassified remainder; already_known there is a lower bound (only classified rows were checked).
